title: EC2 instances, AMIs, and launch templates
hook: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is the boot blueprint; the instance type is the hardware profile. Together they define what runs, how fast, and what it costs.

blocks.text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) provides virtual machines in AWS regions. An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) captures the root volume template — operating system, patches, and baked application bits. Instance types (families like t3, m6i, c7g) encode vCPU, memory, network bandwidth, and optional accelerators. Launch templates version the full launch specification: AMI, type, key pair, network interfaces, storage, tags, and Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) settings.

entries.plainDefinition: Template for the root volume and launch permissions.
entries.example: Amazon Linux 2023 AMI with SSM agent preinstalled.

entries.plainDefinition: Named hardware profile: vCPU, RAM, network, storage options.
Versioned launch spec replacing legacy launch configurations.
entries.example: Version 3 switches AMI after Image Builder pipeline.

entries.plainDefinition: Session-oriented metadata access requiring a PUT token first.
entries.example: HttpTokens: required blocks SSRF from stealing IAM role creds.

blocks.text: Wrong instance family wastes money (GPU for CRUD API) or causes throttling (burstable t3 CPU credits exhausted). AMIs drift without pipelines — golden AMI builds via EC2 Image Builder keep CVE patches consistent. Launch templates are how Auto Scaling Groups and blue/green deploys reference immutable infra versions.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: AMI = what boots, instance type = capacity profile, launch template = versioned launch contract with IMDSv2 required and instance profile for AWS API access.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Select AMI and type
items.body: Pick region-local AMI; match workload to family (compute, memory, burstable).

items.title: Configure networking
items.body: Subnet, security groups, public IP assignment, primary ENI settings in template.

items.title: Attach storage mappings
items.body: Root gp3 volume size, encryption, additional EBS or instance store from type.

items.title: Bootstrap
items.body: User data script runs at first boot — idempotent cloud-init or PowerShell.

diagram.title: Launch template to instance
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  LT[Launch template v2] --> LTspec[AMI + type + SG + EBS]
  LTspec --> Run[RunInstances / ASG]
  Run --> Inst[EC2 instance]
  Inst --> IMDS[IMDSv2 token]
  Inst --> Profile[Instance profile IAM role]

snippet.label: Launch template with IMDSv2
snippet.code:
LaunchTemplate:
  Type: AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate
  Properties:
    LaunchTemplateData:
      ImageId: ami-0abcdef1234567890
      InstanceType: m6i.large
      IamInstanceProfile:
        Arn: !GetAtt InstanceProfile.Arn
      MetadataOptions:
        HttpTokens: required
        HttpEndpoint: enabled
      BlockDeviceMappings:
        - DeviceName: /dev/xvda
          Ebs:
            VolumeSize: 30
            VolumeType: gp3
            Encrypted: true
snippet.explanation: HttpTokens required enforces IMDSv2. Encrypted gp3 root is production baseline.

snippet.label: Launch instance from template
snippet.code:
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --launch-template LaunchTemplateName=web-app,Version=2 \
  --subnet-id subnet-0abc123 \
  --security-group-ids sg-0web456 \
  --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=web-1}]'
snippet.explanation: Template carries AMI and type; subnet and SG can override per launch.

snippet.label: Create AMI from golden instance
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-image \
  --instance-id i-0golden \
  --name "web-app-golden-2026-09-14" \
  --no-reboot
aws ec2 describe-images --owners self --filters "Name=name,Values=web-app-golden-*"
snippet.explanation: Image Builder automates this; manual AMI for labs. no-reboot risks filesystem consistency — prefer staged pipeline.

snippet.label: IMDSv2 token fetch from instance
snippet.explanation: Proves IMDSv2 path. Apps and SDKs use instance profile automatically when configured.

blocks.title: Runtime and deployment parallels
rows: Docker image / VM template — not portable across clouds without rebuild
Discrete instance types — vertical scale = change type
Node process scales vertically until memory cap — no instance type picker
IMDS exposes role credentials and user data
No EC2 metadata — use env vars and secret managers in Node
npm start in Dockerfile CMD — runs every container start

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using long-lived access keys on instances instead of instance profiles. Leaving IMDSv1 enabled on internet-facing apps. Baking secrets into AMIs instead of fetching at boot from Secrets Manager.

blocks.text: Burstable t3/t4g instances accumulate CPU credits — sustained 100% CPU causes throttle visible in CPUSurplusCreditBalance CloudWatch metric. Graviton (c7g/m7g) needs ARM-built binaries. How to prove it in production: CloudWatch agent for mem/disk, SSM Inventory for AMI age, AWS Compute Optimizer rightsizing recommendations, and golden AMI pipeline age alarm > 30 days.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Commitment risk if architecture shifts to containers
Highest cost — only for license or placement rules

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'pick t2.micro for production API' without mentioning CPU credits or network limits. Strong answer: map workload to family, enforce IMDSv2, golden AMI pipeline, instance profile, encrypted EBS.

interviewTakeaways: AMI defines the boot disk template; instance type defines compute, memory, and network capacity.
Launch templates are versioned — prefer them over deprecated launch configurations for ASG integration.
Require IMDSv2 and instance profiles; never embed access keys in user data or AMIs.
60s: AMI + instance type + launch template version = reproducible EC2. IMDSv2 required. Golden AMI pipeline. Instance profile not keys.
Follow-up: how do you roll out a new AMI across an ASG without downtime?
commonPitfalls: Saying AMIs are global — saying that gets you rejected because AMIs are regional; copy across regions for DR.
Strong answer: AMI copy, launch template new version, ASG instance refresh with min healthy 90%.
Embedding database connection strings in user data instead of Secrets Manager.
Using burstable instances for CPU-saturated APIs without credit monitoring.

jsTsCorrelations.note: A Node.js server on EC2 is one OS process tree on a VM you patch and scale via ASG. Unlike serverless, you own the kernel, libc, and long-lived connections.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: Config at boot vs build time
jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript apps often bake env at Docker build; on EC2, user data fetches SSM parameters at boot — similar to runtime config injection but at VM layer not container layer.
